description:
Set one or more properties on a node in a .tscn scene. This is THE tool for changing node properties, including resources. ALWAYS use it (or create_scene/add_node) to change scenes; never edit .tscn files as text.

Values are read according to each property's type:
  • numbers, bools, strings; enums by name ("Nearest", "TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST") or number
  • Vector2/3: {x, y[, z]} or [x, y[, z]]; Color: {r, g, b, a?} (0..1), "#ff8800" or "red"; Rect2: {x, y, width, height}
  • resources (texture, shape, mesh, material, stream, font, ...): a file path "res://icon.png", or an inline resource {"type": "RectangleShape2D", "size": {"x": 32, "y": 16}} whose other keys are its properties (nested resources work)
  • a property of a resource the node holds, via a colon path: {"shape:radius": 12, "material:albedo_color": "red"}
  • null clears a resource property

**All-or-nothing:** every value is checked first and the scene is saved only if every write was accepted. Each write is read back: values Godot adjusted (clamped, wrapped) are listed in `adjusted`; a write Godot ignored is an error. Errors name the property and suggest close names. Scripts: use attach_script. Response: {ok, applied: [{property, old, new}], adjusted?}.

node_path.description: Path to the node (. for root, or relative path)

properties.description: Map of property name (or colon path like "material:albedo_color") -> value. See the tool description for value forms.

scene_path.description: Path to the .tscn scene file, or to a .tres/.res resource file to edit that resource directly (node_path then omitted)

name: set_node_properties
